title: Quantifying evaluation leakage in multi-species gene-disease link prediction: a graded audit and a de-leaked benchmark
description:
Code, de-leaked evaluation splits, and benchmark results accompanying the manuscript "Quantifying evaluation leakage in multi-species gene-disease link prediction: a graded audit and a de-leaked benchmark."

Resource. A graded leakage audit of gene-disease link prediction on a multi-species, Monarch-derived knowledge graph (452,012 nodes; 5,860,539 directed edges; 28 relation types across 8 node categories). The graph is approximately 98.3% Monarch Initiative content augmented with seven curated non-Monarch sources (DGIdb, GWAS Catalog, DrugCentral, Orphadata, Gene2Phenotype, CIViC, DIDA); it is a Monarch-derived knowledge graph, not an equal integration of many independent databases.

Benchmark. Four knowledge-graph-embedding models spanning two families (translational: TransE, RotatE; bilinear: DistMult, ComplEx) and five topological baselines (Random, Common-Neighbors, Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, Preferential-Attachment) are evaluated under one shared ranking harness on 4,228 held-out human gene-disease test edges, across four regimes: R0 (random split), R1 (training edges that directly join held-out pairs removed), R2 (training graph rewired with node degrees preserved), and R3 (cross-species orthology edges removed). Three seeds (42, 1, 7). Full ranking against all diseases (filtered, tail-only) is the primary protocol; ranking against 50 sampled negatives is secondary.

Main findings. Because R2 preserves degree but destroys other structure, the share of R0 MRR it retains estimates the part attainable from degree alone. Under full ranking, KGE models retain 18-30% and overlap heuristics 9-12%, so most performance requires structure beyond degree; against sampled negatives, KGE models retain 63-79%, so sampled ranking overstates the role of degree. For the lowest-degree diseases, R2 removes almost all of the score. R1 lowers KGE MRR by 10-32% (full ranking) but overlap-heuristic MRR by at most 2%, and R3 lowers no method's MRR by more than 1.1%, so the R3 graph is released as a control rather than a correction. Differences are tested by paired bootstrap (100,000 resamples) with Holm correction over 76 comparisons.

Contents. De-leaked splits and split manifest (splits.zip -> data/processed/splits/); per-regime baseline and KGE result JSONs under both protocols, with per-edge reciprocal ranks, the 200-graph permutation null and the multiple-testing results (results.zip -> data/processed/results/); per-source provenance (provenance.zip); generators for the revised manuscript's tables and figures (scripts/make_revision_assets.py, multiple_testing.py, hub_cap_analysis.py, overlap_lowdegree.py, pool_exclusion.py) and for the first submission's (scripts/make_tables.py, make_figures.py), all reading only the frozen result JSONs (no hand-entered numbers); and a one-command regeneration script (run_all.sh / run_all.ps1). All runs use fixed seeds; paths are repo-relative with no secrets or hard-coded machine paths.
